answer: To resist sybil attacks, each agent must periodically produce and burn a unique nectar token derived from a scarce, non-parallelizable oasis of compute capacity that only one physical host can harbor at a time. An attacker spawning many fakes must therefore acquire and maintain that many separate physical machines, each contributing its own nectar, making the marginal cost of each extra identity equal to the full hardware and power expense rather than near-zero software clones.
